name: Is it better to replace an entire wall's baseboard or just the damaged section?

mainEntity.name: Is it better to replace an entire wall's baseboard or just the damaged section?

acceptedAnswer.text: Generally, it's more cost-effective and efficient to replace only the damaged section of baseboard, provided a matching material and finish can be achieved. However, if the damage is extensive across a large portion of the wall, or if the existing baseboards are severely outdated, mismatched, or difficult to blend seamlessly with new sections, replacing the entire wall's baseboard can result in a more uniform and aesthetically pleasing outcome. Consider the overall appearance and potential for future repairs.
acceptedAnswer.description: Replacing only damaged sections is cost-effective if a match is possible. Replacing an entire wall's baseboard is better for extensive damage or if a seamless match is difficult.
